name: Ramp
text: We should implement a visible server-side skip link at the top of every page. This ensures that users relying on keyboard navigation can easily bypass repetitive content and access main sections quickly. The trade-off is that it may slightly alter the visual layout on page load, but the enhanced accessibility justifies this change, making navigation smoother for everyone.

name: Reader
text: A visible server-side skip link risks pushing down content below the fold, hurting mobile users and those with small screens. A hidden skip link that only appears on keyboard focus meets WCAG without layout disruption. Settle it by testing both versions with real keyboard users—if the hidden version works, drop the visible one.

name: Ramp
text:
We should use a hidden skip link that only appears on keyboard focus. This meets WCAG without pushing content below the fold, protecting mobile and small-screen users. The trade-off is that sighted keyboard users won’t see the skip link until they tab, but that’s acceptable since keyboard users expect to tab through focusable elements. Testing with real keyboard users will confirm if the hidden version works better than a visible one.

name: Reader
text: A hidden skip link may confuse users who are less experienced with keyboard navigation, as they might not realize it's there until they tab through. This could diminish the user experience for some, especially if they expect to see such navigation immediately. Testing both options with a diverse group of users, including those new to keyboard navigation, would provide clearer insights into user preferences and effectiveness.
